description: UNSAFE is a Python model for estimating property-level flood damage while representing uncertainty in building exposure and vulnerability. The developer repository describes adding uncertain parameters to the National Structure Inventory and combining alternative depth-damage functions with inundation-model output. These calculations can compare flood-risk and adaptation assessments without treating building attributes or damage curves as certain. Its documented applications focus on United States buildings; spatial coverage follows the selected structures and flood scenario. Code and worked examples are free on GitHub under BSD-2-Clause. A limitation is that the published implementation covers residential properties of up to three storeys. Stochastic sampling can change individual results, and parts of the API documentation and automated testing remain under development. The existing data-usace-national-structure-inventory is its named building-data input. This review checked public metadata and examples described in the README without obtaining structure data or reproducing damage estimates.
inputs: Uncertain exposure parameters and depth-damage functions
name: UNSAFE flood-risk uncertainty model
notes: G5 G5-0091. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
outputs: Property-level flood-damage estimates under exposure and vulnerability uncertainty
